newsitem.title: SWEDEN: NCC sees Nordic construction up 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: NCC sees Nordic construction up 1997/98.

text.p: Sweden's second largest building company, NCC, on Tuesday said its profits doubled in 1996 and it saw the Nordic construction market growing by two percent in 1997 and 1998.
Posting a 1996 profit after financial items of 462 million crowns ($62.5 million) compared to 230 million in 1995, NCC said sales rose to 22.99 billion crowns from 16.57 billion a year earlier.
"Total construction in Sweden rose slightly in 1996, marking the first increase since the beginning of the recession in the industry," NCC said in a statement.
"On the whole, total growth in the Nordic construction market in 1996 was three percent.
"The market is expected to increase by two percent in 1997 and 1998."
NCC said demand for Swedish office properties has recovered in the real estate market.
"Market conditions are strongest in major cities, where rent levels have risen, while the trend in other segments is static," the company said.
Operating profit after depreciation rose to 866 million crowns from 695 million, the company said.
Profits were boosted by increased earnings from NCC's construction and real estate operations and an improvement in ferry company Silja Line's results, in which NCC holds a 33 percent stake.
Excluding shares in losses of associated companies profit after financial items amounted to 522 million, up from 424 million, NCC said.
NCC proposed to raise its dividend to 1.50 crowns per share, from 1.25 crowns.
Construction order intake rose 17 percent to 18 billion crowns from 15.4 billion. Orders received outside Sweden accounted for 6.8 billion, up from 2.6 billion, the company said.
Earlier in the month, NCC made a public offer for Swedish rival Siab and announced it will spin off NK Cityfastigheter AB and list it on the Stockholm Stock Exchange.
On Tuesday it said it would sell 60-75 percent of NK Cityfastigheter AB, a department store and shopping mall properties company, and set the price range to 55-64 crowns a share.
